items.title: Live: Trump says US 'no longer' needs NATO allies, Australia in Iran war
items.description: Donald Trump says the US "do not need the help of anyone" in the war against Iran, calling out NATO allies and Australia in a fiery social media post. Follow live.

items.title: As Israel invades Lebanon, a long occupation could lead to total collapse
items.description: Israel is moving more troops into southern Lebanon ahead of what some fear will be a long occupation, and experts warn further destabilisation could threaten the country's existence.

items.title: Why Israel is trying to dismantle Hezbollah by its own means
items.description: As Israel's intense bombardment continues into a third week, Lebanon's war-weary population and cash-strapped government are wondering when the fighting will stop.

items.title: Middle East war forces pharmaceutical companies to divert critical medicines
items.description: The Middle East war is forcing major pharmaceutical companies to divert critical medicines away from one of the world's most important trade routes, to ensure there are no supply issues in Australia.

items.title: Who is Ali Larijani, the man whose power grew during Mideast war?
items.description: When Israeli and US strikes killed Ayatollah Ali Khamenei at the start of the Middle East war, Iran's security chief Ali Larijani became even more powerful than he had been for decades.

items.title: Historical IVF mix-up discovery raises questions about Australian industry
items.description: Fertility experts say the discovery of an IVF mix-up at Royal North Shore Hospital in 1995 could be the tip of the iceberg as more Australians research their parentage.

items.title: RBA governor warns of the recession we might have to have
items.description: Is the RBA fighting last year's inflation war with its latest interest rate hike? Whatever the case may be, Australians are bracing for even more economic pain.

items.title: To fix the generation gap, Labor may have to leave the grandfathers behind
items.description: A Senate committee report into the capital gains tax was authored by the Greens but littered with clues about Labor's plans.

items.title: Rare triple-hit cyclone possible to impact Qld, NT and WA
items.description: The last Australian triple landfall system was Severe Tropical Cyclone Ingrid more than two decades ago.

items.title: Avoid sugar hits, economists warn, as rate hike pain rolls out
items.description: Economist are urging the government make brave budget calls as Australian households prepare to sweat through another rate rise.

items.title: 'Deeply upsetting': Grace Tame criticised for comments on October 7 attacks
items.description: Australia's Israeli embassy has criticised comments Grace Tame made about reports of sexual violence perpetrated by terrorist group Hamas.

items.title: Matildas book place in Asian Cup final with lion-hearted win over China
items.description: Goals from Caitlin Foord and Sam Kerr fire the Matildas to a 2-1 semifinal victory over China and a shot at a first continental crown since 2010.

items.title: Fake cash flooding into Australian market as seizures rise 700 per cent
items.description: Cash may have declined in use during COVID but the use of it has steadied since. But technology has also opened a door to fake cash and its being seized now at much higher levels.

items.title: 'A slow burning disaster': National court transcript service calls in administrators
items.description: Four weeks after the ABC revealed sensitive court files were being accessed offshore in a potential risk to national security, the company responsible for the breach has entered into voluntary administration.

items.title: Behind Melbourne Museum's shiny facade sits a world hidden from view
items.description: Museums display only a fraction of their collection so we went behind the scenes at the Melbourne Museum to find the untold stories kept from public view.

items.title: This 'tender and dark' comedy might inspire you to quit your job
items.description: This dark comedy takes aim at capitalism and corporate work culture, but it also finds hope in the relationships between everyday people.

items.title: Quiz: Do you have the frequent flyers points to pass our test?
items.description: Which country’s currency is called the quetzal? And what is Thailand's Songkran festival best known for?

items.title: The 'new hysteria is anxiety': Teens push back against medical bias
items.description: Young women have detailed their experiences being dismissed and misdiagnosed as chronic pain sufferers. Now, they're teaching others how to advocate for their health.

items.title: Report finds 'significant and sustained shift' in support for salmon industry
items.description: A CSIRO report has found Tasmania's salmon farming industry has experienced a "significant and sustained shift" away from strong community support it experienced a decade ago.

items.title: Fuel shortages hit tipping point as WA miner stands down most workers
items.description: Fuel shortages linked to the Middle East war are forcing a WA gold miner to stand down workers, exposing how smaller operators are being squeezed while major miners maintain supply.

items.title: 'Lacks rationality': Japanese court rules on women's right to sterilisation
items.description: A law in Japan bans childless women from accessing voluntary sterilisation. Now a Tokyo judge has found it "lacks rationality" and should be debated.

items.title: Kyle Sandilands considering 'many options' amid doubt over radio future
items.description: Radio broadcaster Kyle Sandilands says he is considering "many options" after being taken off-air for insulting his co-host and friend of almost 30 years Jackie "O" Henderson.

items.title: Density push to allow for 20-storey towers in Melbourne's north
items.description: The Victorian government has released its final planning controls for 25 activity centres in Melbourne, with tweaks meaning lower height limits in parts of Kew and Oakleigh and higher heights in parts of Coburg and Brunswick.

items.title: Banksy's real identity revealed in new investigation
items.description: An in-depth investigation drawing on court files, photos and public records reports the world-famous anonymous artist is a Bristol-born man who later adopted a new identity.

items.title: 'We have exciting days ahead': Danish royals arrive in Melbourne
items.description: The king and queen of Denmark will arrive in Melbourne for the first of two days of royal engagements as part of their Australian state visit.
